QF.id: AIFM CII Investment Process and Governance_11

question.text: 'Indus Growth Category II AIF' holds 20% in an investee company; the founders hold 60%. The tag-along (co-sale) right held by the AIF means:

answer.text: If the AIF sells, the founders MUST also sell to the same buyer
If the founders sell to a buyer, the AIF can require that buyer to also purchase an equivalent percentage of the AIF's shares at the same price and terms
The AIF can sell its shares only through a SEBI-registered broker
The AIF can block any sale by the founders for 5 years

explanation.text: **The Logic:** Tag-along (co-sale) protects MINORITY investors. When the majority/founders sell, the minority can 'tag' along on the same price and terms for an equivalent percentage. It makes the founder shares harder to sell cleanly, protecting the AIF against being left with a new controlling shareholder it did not vet. **The Trap:** Option A describes DRAG-ALONG, not tag-along. Blocking for 5 years is a lock-in. Broker requirement is fictional. **Cross-Exam Context:** XIX-C tests tag vs drag identically. XIX-A doesn't cover investee-level exit mechanics. **Manager's Pro-Tip:** Tag-along without a 'pro-rata participation' cap lets a large AIF exit 100% alongside a small founder sale — negotiate a pro-rata cap so the founder can do small partial liquidity events without dragging the fund.
